---
title: "Getting Started"
---

::: {.callout-warning}
**Preview install.** Use the source checkout for the current review build. A
package-index release has not been published, and the MLPerf EDU component
license remains a release gate.
:::

MLPerf EDU targets Python 3.10 or newer and uses
[uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) for a locked local environment. A GPU is not
required. PyTorch uses Apple MPS or CUDA when available.

## Install From a Checkout

```bash
git clone https://github.com/harvard-edge/cs249r_book
cd cs249r_book/mlperf-edu
uv sync --locked --extra dev
uv run mlperf doctor
```

`mlperf doctor` checks Python, PyTorch, the accelerator, caches, and the
workload registry. Resolve any failed required check before continuing.

## Run the Smoke Contract

```bash
uv run mlperf validate smoke --output-dir submissions/first-smoke
```

The smoke preset exercises the fast functional path and grades its outputs. It
is not a benchmark score. Runtime depends on the machine and installed
backends.

## Explore the Registry

```bash
uv run mlperf list
uv run mlperf list --suite language
uv run mlperf show causal-language-modeling
uv run mlperf info --dataset tinyshakespeare
```

The same information appears under [Benchmarks](benchmarks/index.qmd). Those
pages are generated from the registry consumed by the CLI.

## Run One Candidate Benchmark

```bash
uv run mlperf fetch --workload causal-language-modeling --profile max
uv run mlperf run --workload causal-language-modeling --profile max \
  --mode training \
  --output-dir submissions/causal-review
```

`fetch` prepares and verifies assets before measurement. `run` writes
timestamped JSON, HTML, and CSV reports plus a `.provd.json` provenance
manifest. The HTML dashboard opens automatically and leads with the run
metric, target decision, configuration, model lineage, and provenance. Use
`--no-open-report` on a headless machine. Treat the result as a project
candidate until its quality,
provenance, asset-policy, and release-workflow checks all pass.

Continue with the [running guide](guide/running.qmd) for profiles, selection,
and power telemetry, or open a [benchmark page](benchmarks/index.qmd) for
registry-derived commands.
